sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or give reasons).

questions.q: Write True or False. (i) The sludge left after biogas production is a waste product with no use. (ii) Using light-coloured walls can reduce the lighting requirement of a room by up to 40%. (iii) A major advantage of a solar cooker is that it requires constant attention while cooking. (iv) Driving a tractor in the wrong gear can decrease work efficiency by 50%.
questions.answer: (i) False: it is an excellent fertiliser. (ii) True. (iii) False: it needs no constant attention. (iv) True.

questions.q: State True or False. (a) Nuclear fuel is a renewable source of energy. (b) A pressure cooker helps to save time. (c) Geothermal energy is the solar heat energy trapped by rocks. (d) A small refrigerator consumes less power than a big refrigerator.
questions.answer: (a) False: it is non-renewable. (b) True. (c) True. (d) True.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) Biogas is produced by fermentation of ________ in the absence of air. (b) The motto 'S.O.S.' means Save on ________.
Match Column A with Column B. A: (a) Solar cell (b) Windmill. B: (i) Electricity from wind (ii) Electricity from daylight (iii) Gas from manure.
Separate renewable (R) and non-renewable (NR) sources: sunlight, petroleum, steam, charcoal, wind, nuclear fuel.
questions.answer: R: sunlight, wind. NR: petroleum, steam (produced by burning fuels), charcoal, nuclear fuel.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What are the four advantages of a solar cooker over a gas stove?
questions.answer: It reduces fuel cost and is totally safe, with no fire or leaking gas. It needs no constant attention and can cook up to four dishes at a time.

questions.q: Why is it important to conserve energy? Give two reasons.
questions.answer: Demand for energy exceeds the supply because of population, industry and automation. Fuels like oil and gas are limited and may run out in our lifetime.

questions.q: List two uses of biogas.
questions.answer: It is used for cooking and lighting. It can also pump water and run small motors.

questions.q: What is the difference between a large hydroelectric project and a micro-hydel project?
questions.answer: A big project uses a big river and needs heavy investment. A micro-hydel project uses smaller rivers, costs less and supplies local remote areas.

questions.q: Mention two ways of saving fuel while cooking.
questions.answer: Use a pressure cooker with separators to cook many dishes together, and use a solar cooker. Keep burner holes clean and use a small burner for a small vessel.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the importance of conserving energy (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Demand exceeds supply, so reducing demand is the only option. (ii) Energy saved is energy generated and reduces power cuts. (iii) Fuels are limited: natural gas about 30 years, oil about 50 and coal about 280.

questions.q: List the suggestions to a housewife for conserving energy at home (any three).
questions.answer: (i) Switch off lights and fans when leaving a room and use tubelights or CFLs. (ii) Use a pressure cooker, a solar cooker and small burners for small vessels. (iii) Use the refrigerator of the right size without opening it often, and use ISI marked appliances.

questions.q: Explain how energy can be saved on the farm (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Maintain tractors well and prevent diesel leakage. (ii) Drive in the right gear and switch off the engine when not in use. (iii) Keep the air filter clean and plan digging lengthwise.

questions.q: Explain the advantages of non-conventional sources of energy (three points).
questions.answer: (i) They give a never-ending supply and are easily available. (ii) They are pollution free. (iii) They are locally produced, so low distribution cost, and small-scale units give jobs.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the energy options for the future with their advantages.
questions.answer: (i) Biogas from animal manure is a cheap fuel for cooking and lighting, and the sludge is a fertiliser. (ii) A solar cooker saves fuel and is safe. (iii) Solar cells give lighting and solar heating warms water and dries crops. (iv) Micro-hydel projects supply remote areas with low investment. (v) Wind energy is free and non-polluting and suits hilly areas. (vi) All are renewable, pollution free and give local jobs.
